unit.title: Diagnose & repair faults in electrical equipment

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A bench grinder from a Kingston machine shop is brought in marked 'not working'. What should you do first?
options: Strip the motor down to look at the windings
Ask the user what happened and when it stopped
Order a new motor so the job is not delayed
Plug it in at the bench to hear what it does

questions.stem: There is no maker's data for an old pump motor. How can you best find out what its normal winding readings should be?
options: Guess from the motor's size and its colour
Use the readings from any motor in the store
Assume every winding should read zero ohms
Compare it with an identical motor known to be good

questions.stem: Why is changing parts at random until a machine works a poor way to repair it?
options: It wastes parts and the real cause may stay hidden
It is always slower than reading the whole manual first
Spare parts may only be fitted by the maker's agent
The machine's warranty forbids changing any parts

questions.stem: You are about to repair a 220 V concrete mixer that plugs into a site outlet. How should you isolate it?
options: Switch it off at its own switch and then start work
Ask a co-worker to stand beside the outlet for you
Unplug it and keep the plug under your control
Turn off the site lights fed from the same board

questions.stem: A standby generator with automatic starting needs a repair. As well as isolating its output, what else must be done?
options: Fill the fuel tank so it cannot run dry during the work
Leave it in automatic so it is ready if the power fails
Lock its controls off so that it cannot start by itself
Open the canopy doors so the engine cools down faster

questions.stem: A power factor correction capacitor bank has been isolated. Why must you still wait and prove it is discharged before touching it?
options: Capacitors can hold a dangerous charge after isolation
The capacitors need time to fill up with oil again
Its fuses must cool down before they can be removed
The energy meter needs time to reset after switch-off

questions.stem: A 220/24 V control transformer gives no output. With it isolated and disconnected, its primary winding reads open circuit. What does this mean?
options: The secondary winding has a short between its turns
The supply to the panel is at the wrong frequency
The transformer is fine; the fuse must be at fault
The primary is broken, so the unit must be replaced

questions.stem: A small transformer gets very hot even when nothing is connected to its secondary. What is the most likely fault?
options: The load on its secondary is far too large
Shorted turns inside one of its windings
The secondary fuse is rated too low
The output terminals have come loose

questions.stem: A transformer's primary has 1 100 turns and is fed at 220 V. Its secondary has 120 turns. What should the secondary voltage be?
An angle grinder sparks heavily round its commutator and has lost power. What is the most likely cause?
options: The disc guard is fitted the wrong way round
The cable is a little longer than the old one
Worn brushes or a dirty, worn commutator
The on/off switch has been used too often

questions.stem: An electric drill only works when its cable is bent at one spot near the handle. What is the fault?
options: The brushes have worn right down to their springs
A conductor in the flex is broken near the entry
The chuck key has been left in the drill chuck
The trigger's speed control is set much too low

questions.stem: Why must new carbon brushes be the size and grade the tool maker specifies?
options: Other grades of brush cannot be bought in Jamaica
Only the maker's grade is the right colour for it
Any brush will work, as long as the label matches
The wrong grade can spark and wear the commutator

questions.stem: After a pump and its motor were put back on their base, the motor vibrates badly and the coupling gets warm. What is the most likely cause?
options: The motor's supply frequency is too high
The pump is moving too little water
The motor's nameplate has been painted over
The motor and pump shafts are out of line

questions.stem: A motor's bearings ran hot soon after a worker packed them completely full of grease. Why?
options: Grease must never be used in electric motors
Too much grease churns and makes heat
The grease made the windings short out
The bearings had too little grease left

questions.stem: With a three-phase motor running, the instructor measures phase currents of 12 A, 12 A and 17 A. What do these readings point to?
options: An unbalance in the supply or the windings
A motor running at exactly its rated load
A fault in the motor's cooling fan only
Normal running, as the currents always differ

questions.stem: A motor stored for months in a damp shed gives a low insulation resistance reading. What is usually done?
options: Run it on full load to dry it out quickly
Scrap the motor at once and order another
Dry it out as the maker says, then test again
Paint the windings with varnish while still wet

questions.stem: Why keep a record of a motor's insulation resistance readings taken over several years?
options: So the motor can be sold later for a higher price
A falling trend warns of failure before it happens
So the tester's battery life can be checked
The readings are needed to set the motor's speed

questions.stem: In a polarisation index (PI) test on a large motor, which two readings are compared?
options: The readings taken at the start of two different days
The reading at 500 V and the reading at 1 000 V
The readings between line and neutral only
The readings after 10 minutes and after 1 minute

questions.stem: Unless the maker says otherwise, which insulation test voltage is usually used on 110/220 V equipment?
options: 50 V DC
250 V AC
500 V DC
5 000 V DC

questions.stem: A contactor buzzes loudly and chatters when it pulls in. Which is a likely cause?
options: Low coil voltage or dirty magnet faces
The main contacts are new and very clean
The motor it feeds is only lightly loaded
The overload relay is set slightly high

questions.stem: A motor keeps running after STOP is pressed. With the circuit isolated, the contactor's main contacts are found stuck together. What is this fault called?
options: Welded contacts
A loose neutral
Single phasing
An open-circuit coil

questions.stem: A star-delta starter starts the motor in star, but it never changes over to delta and then trips. Where would you look first?
options: At the motor's bearings and its cooling fan
At the incoming supply cable's insulation
At the timer and the delta contactor circuit
At the colours of the starter's push-buttons

questions.stem: The AC coil of a solenoid valve has burnt out twice in one month. What is the most likely cause?
options: The valve is fitted on a water line
The coil is switched on and off many times by a timer
The coil's voltage is on its label
The plunger sticks, so the coil draws high current

questions.stem: An electric oven's light and fan work, but it never heats. The element reads correctly when isolated. Which part is next most likely to be at fault?
options: The hinge on the oven door
The thermostat or its contacts
The holder for the oven light
The cooling fan's motor

questions.stem: A heater is rated 220 V, 1 500 W. Using R = V² ÷ P, about what should its element read when isolated and cold?
A standby generator runs at its correct speed but gives no output voltage. Which part should be checked?
options: The engine's fuel filter
The voltage regulator (AVR) and excitation
The level gauge and float switch on the main fuel tank
The exhaust silencer

questions.stem: On load, a standby generator's output frequency falls to 47 Hz. What is the most likely cause?
options: The engine is running too slowly
The voltage regulator is set too high
The output cables are too large
The load is all lighting and heaters

questions.stem: Why must a standby generator's changeover switch be interlocked?
options: So the generator can run at a higher speed
So the fuel lasts longer during a power cut
So the building can use both supplies at once
So it can never feed back into the power lines

questions.stem: A UPS shows its batteries as fully charged, but it shuts down a minute after the mains fails. What is the most likely cause?
options: The UPS cooling fan is blocked with dust
The batteries have lost their capacity
The UPS has too little load connected
The output sockets are dusty inside

questions.stem: Why must there be good ventilation and no sparks near lead-acid batteries on charge?
options: The acid boils away if the room is warm
The batteries need fresh air to make electricity
Sparks make the batteries charge too fast
Charging gives off hydrogen, which can explode

questions.stem: A metal-cased (Class I) power tool fails its earth continuity test. What is the likely fault?
options: A broken or loose earth conductor
Worn carbon brushes in the motor
A blunt cutting blade or drill bit
A cracked plastic cover on the handle

questions.stem: A double-insulated (Class II) drill is being checked. Which test is NOT done on it?
options: A visual check of the case and the cable
An insulation resistance test
An earth continuity test
A check of the plug and its pins

questions.stem: A failed motor must be replaced with a new one. Which details must the new motor match?
options: Only its kW rating and its paint colour
Only its price and how soon it can be delivered
Its kW, voltage, speed, frame and enclosure
Only its shaft length and its weight

questions.stem: When is a failed motor usually sent to a specialist rewinder?
options: When a winding is open or shorted to earth
When its terminal box cover is missing
When its paint is faded and scratched
When a terminal screw is slightly loose

questions.stem: Why must a blown HRC fuse be replaced with one of the same type and breaking capacity?
options: So the fuse holder stays the same colour
So the fuse is easier to remove next time
Because fuses of higher rating cost less
So it can clear a large fault current safely

questions.stem: A replacement motor overload relay has been fitted. What should its setting normally be based on?
options: The rating of the main breaker
The full-load current on the nameplate
The motor's starting current
Twice the current rating of the motor's supply cable

questions.stem: A pump motor's bearings have failed three times in six months. What should you do this time?
options: Find out why, such as belt tension or alignment
Fit the same bearings again and log the job
Fit a bigger motor so the bearings last longer
Tell the client that bearings always fail fast

questions.stem: You have reconnected a motor's terminal box after a repair. Which dead tests confirm the work before anyone energises it?
options: A check that the paint is dry and the cover is clean
A sound test by tapping the frame with a spanner
Continuity, insulation resistance and earth checks
A test run with the cover off to watch the terminals

questions.stem: At the Centre, who energises a repaired machine for its function test?
options: The trainee who did the repair
Any trainee who has passed Level 2
The client who owns the machine
Only the instructor

questions.stem: Which entry in a repair report is most useful to the next technician?
options: The machine was fixed and now works fine
Fault, cause, parts fitted and test readings
The time the technician took for lunch
The name of the shop the tools came from

questions.stem: You lead two junior technicians on a repair. One says he has isolated the motor. What should you do?
options: Trust him and start the work straight away
Ask the other junior to start the work instead
Switch the breaker on and off to check it
Check his lock, tag and dead test yourself

questions.stem: A key spare part has a three-week delivery time and the client needs the machine daily. What should you do first?
options: Tell the client and agree a safe temporary plan
Fit any part that looks similar until it arrives
Leave the job and stop answering the client's calls
Bypass the faulty part so the machine still runs

questions.stem: A DC shunt motor on a training rig races far above its normal speed when the instructor runs it. Which fault could cause this?
options: A heavy load on the motor shaft
A low armature supply voltage
An open circuit in the shunt field
Brushes that are very well bedded in

questions.stem: A pump should start 10 seconds after a fan, but both start together. With the panel isolated, what should be checked?
options: The bearings of the pump motor
The timer's setting, function and wiring
The angle of the fan blades
The size of the incoming main supply cable to the panel

questions.stem: How should old lead-acid batteries removed from a UPS be disposed of?
options: As hazardous waste, through an approved recycler
In the normal skip with the other site rubbish
Buried in a hole at the back of the workshop
Emptied into the yard drain, then put in the normal bin

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: On a universal motor, what is the segmented copper part of the armature that the carbon brushes rub on?
What do the letters AVR stand for on a generator?
A transformer's primary has 880 turns and is fed at 220 V. Its secondary has 48 turns. What is the secondary voltage, in volts?
A 110 V heater is rated 1 000 W. Using R = V² ÷ P, what should its element read, in ohms, to one decimal place?
What is it called when a generator sends power back into the power company's lines?
In what unit is insulation resistance usually read? Give the word or the symbol.
What is the test tool called that finds shorted turns in a motor armature by using an AC magnetic field?
Which tool is used to draw a bearing off a motor shaft without hammering it?
In a star-delta starter, in which connection does the motor start?
Which class of equipment is double insulated and has no earth conductor? Give the class.
What is the copper ring set into the magnet face of an AC contactor that stops it humming and chattering?
What is the arrangement called that stops two contactors, such as the forward and reverse contactors, from closing at the same time?
Which gas, able to explode, is given off by lead-acid batteries while they charge?
Using speed (rpm) = 120 × frequency ÷ number of poles, at what speed must a 4-pole generator run to give 50 Hz?
What one word names the difference between an induction motor's synchronous speed and the actual speed of its rotor?

essays.stem: A 220/24 V control transformer in a pump panel gives no output. Describe how you would find the fault using dead tests, and say what each result would tell you.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would isolate the panel, lock it off, tag it and prove it dead with a tester checked before and after use. I would check the fuses on the primary and secondary sides with a continuity test; a blown fuse would mean I must also look for the cause, such as a short in the 24 V control wiring, before replacing it. Next I would disconnect the transformer and measure the resistance of each winding. The primary should show a low but definite reading, and the secondary a lower reading still. An open-circuit reading on either winding means that winding is broken and the transformer must be replaced. A reading far lower than a known good transformer of the same type may point to shorted turns, which often show as overheating or burn marks. I would then do an insulation resistance test between the windings and from each winding to the core and frame; a low reading means the insulation has failed. If all tests pass, the fault is elsewhere, for example in the wiring or terminals, and I would check those.
markingPoints: Isolates, locks off and proves dead with a checked tester
Checks primary and secondary fuses and looks for the cause of a blown fuse
Measures winding resistance and explains open circuit and low readings
Does insulation tests between windings and to the frame
Says what to check next if the transformer passes

essays.stem: An angle grinder sparks heavily at its brushes and has lost power. Describe how you would diagnose and repair it, and the checks you would make before it is used again.
essays.modelAnswer: I would unplug the grinder and keep the plug under my control. I would inspect the cable, plug, case and guard for damage. Then I would remove the brush caps or covers and check the carbon brushes; brushes worn short, chipped or sticking in their holders cause poor contact and heavy sparking. I would inspect the commutator: it should be smooth and clean, not burnt, pitted or with raised segments. A dirty commutator can be cleaned as the maker allows; a badly worn one needs the armature replaced or skimmed by a specialist. If one area of the commutator is burnt, I would suspect a shorted or open armature coil and test the armature on a growler. I would also check the bearings and gears for wear, because a tight bearing makes the motor draw more current. I would fit brushes of the maker's size and grade and let them bed in. Before use, I would do an insulation test and, for a Class I tool, an earth continuity test, and label and record the result.
markingPoints: Unplugs and keeps control of the plug, and inspects the outside first
Checks the brushes for wear and sticking
Inspects the commutator and tests the armature, for example on a growler
Checks bearings and gears, and fits the maker's brushes
Insulation and earth continuity tests, labelling and recording

essays.stem: The bearings of a belt-driven ventilation fan motor at a factory in Spanish Town keep failing every few months. Explain how you would find and fix the root cause.
essays.modelAnswer: Replacing the bearings each time treats only the symptom, so I would look for the reason they fail. I would read the maintenance records to see how often they fail, which bearing goes and what was done before. With the fan isolated and locked off, I would inspect the old bearings: signs such as discoloured grease, rust, a worn track on one side or pitting can point to overheating, water, misalignment or electrical damage. I would check the belt tension with the method the maker gives, as an over-tight belt overloads the bearing nearest the pulley. I would check pulley alignment with a straight edge or alignment tool. I would check the greasing: the type, the amount and how often, because too much grease and too little both cause heat. I would also look at the mounting, loose bolts, an unbalanced fan blade and dust or moisture getting in. Once I find the cause, I would correct it, fit new bearings correctly, record the findings and set a check in the maintenance plan.
markingPoints: Explains that the root cause must be found, not just the symptom treated
Uses records and inspects the failed bearings
Checks belt tension and pulley alignment
Checks the greasing, balance, mounting and contamination
Corrects the cause, records it and plans follow-up checks

essays.stem: Describe how you would carry out an insulation resistance test on a 220 V single-phase motor, and how you would judge and use the results.
essays.modelAnswer: I would isolate the motor, lock off, tag and prove it dead with a tester checked before and after use. I would disconnect the supply cable at the motor terminals and disconnect or bridge any capacitor or electronic parts that could be damaged by the test voltage. I would check the insulation tester and its leads. Using the test voltage the maker states, usually 500 V DC for 110/220 V equipment, I would test from the windings to the motor frame, and between separate windings where they can be split. I would keep the test on for a steady time, such as one minute, and then discharge the windings before touching them. I would compare the readings with the maker's minimum, the figure the Centre gives and the motor's earlier readings. A low reading may mean moisture or damaged insulation; I would dry the motor as the maker says and retest. If it stays low, it needs rewinding. I would record each reading, with the temperature, so the trend can be followed.
markingPoints: Safe isolation and proving dead
Disconnects the cable and protects capacitors or electronics
Correct test voltage and connections, and discharges afterwards
Judges results against the maker's figure and past readings
Explains drying out or rewinding, and records results for trends

essays.stem: During a power cut at a guest house, the standby generator runs but the building gets no power. Explain how you would find the fault safely and what you must not do.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would read the generator and transfer switch displays and note any alarms or fault codes, without opening anything. I would check that the generator is producing the right voltage and frequency on its own meters. If it is not, the fault is on the generator side, for example the voltage regulator, the excitation or the output breaker, which may have tripped. If the generator output is correct, the fault is likely in the automatic transfer switch, its controller, its sensing wiring or the transfer contactor. Before any panel is opened, the generator must be stopped and locked off so that it cannot start by itself, its start battery isolated if the maker says so, and the mains side isolated as well, because power can return at any time. Each part is then proved dead with a tester checked before and after use. I must never bypass or link out the transfer switch or interlock, because the generator could feed back into the power company's lines and kill a line worker.
markingPoints: Reads displays and alarms first
Decides whether the fault is in the generator or the transfer switch
Stops and locks off the generator and prevents automatic start
Isolates the mains side and proves dead with a checked tester
Never bypasses the interlock, because of back-feed danger

essays.stem: A UPS that protects the computers in a Mandeville office now shuts down soon after the mains fails. Explain how you would find the cause, and the safety points when working on its batteries.
essays.modelAnswer: I would read the UPS display and event log for alarms such as 'replace battery' or overload. I would check the connected load against the UPS rating, as too much load shortens the run time. I would find the battery age from the label or records; many sealed lead-acid batteries need replacing after a few years, sooner in hot rooms. With the client's agreement, I would shut down and isolate the UPS as the maker says, remembering that the batteries stay live. I would inspect the batteries for swelling, leaks, corrosion and loose links, and measure each battery's voltage. A battery much lower than the others shows a failed unit. A load test or the UPS's own battery test shows the real capacity. Safety points: battery terminals can give very large currents, so I would use insulated tools, remove rings and watches, and never lay tools on the batteries. Charging gives off hydrogen, so there must be ventilation and no sparks. I would wear eye protection and gloves and recycle old batteries as hazardous waste.
markingPoints: Reads the display or log and checks the load against the rating
Considers battery age and inspects the batteries
Measures battery voltages or uses a battery test to find weak units
Batteries stay live: insulated tools, no jewellery, no tools on top
Hydrogen ventilation, PPE and correct disposal

essays.stem: Explain how a star-delta starter works. Then describe how you would find the fault when the motor starts in star but trips instead of changing to delta.
essays.modelAnswer: A star-delta starter reduces the starting current of a three-phase motor. When START is pressed, the main contactor and the star contactor close, so the windings are connected in star and each gets a lower voltage. After a set time, the timer opens the star contactor and closes the delta contactor, so each winding gets the full line voltage and the motor runs normally. The star and delta contactors are interlocked so they cannot close together. If the motor starts in star but trips instead of changing over, the fault is likely in the changeover. I would isolate the panel, lock off and prove it dead with a checked tester. Using the schematic, I would check the timer's setting and its contacts, the delta contactor coil for open circuit, and the interlock contacts on the star contactor. I would check the wiring and terminals in that part of the control circuit, and that the overload is set correctly. After repair, the instructor or authorised person would carry out the function test.
markingPoints: Explains reduced starting current and the star connection at start
Explains the timer changeover to delta and the interlock
Safe isolation and use of the schematic
Checks the timer, delta contactor coil and interlock contacts
Function test by the instructor or authorised person

essays.stem: A 7.5 kW pump motor at a hotel has a winding that is shorted to earth. Explain how you would decide whether to have it rewound or replaced, and what a replacement must match.
essays.modelAnswer: I would first confirm the fault with an insulation test and winding resistance tests, and check the bearings, shaft and frame. Then I would compare the choices. Rewinding may be cheaper for a large or special motor, but it takes time and the quality depends on the rewinder. A new motor may be quicker if one is in stock, and new motors are often more efficient, which saves on electricity bills. I would get prices and delivery times for both, ask how long the hotel can be without the pump, and check whether there is a standby pump. I would consider the motor's age and its history; an old motor that has failed before is a poor choice to rewind. A replacement must match the power, voltage, phase and frequency of 50 Hz, the speed, the frame size and shaft, the mounting, the enclosure and IP rating, and the duty. I would give the client a clear written recommendation with the costs, and record the decision.
markingPoints: Confirms the fault and checks the mechanical condition
Compares cost, time and quality of rewinding and replacement
Considers downtime, standby equipment, age and efficiency
Lists what a replacement must match
Gives the client a clear written recommendation

essays.stem: You lead a team of two junior technicians repairing faulty equipment at a factory. Explain how you would keep the work safe and make sure the repairs are done right.
essays.modelAnswer: Before work starts I would hold a short briefing on the jobs, the hazards and the isolation needed. I would give each junior tasks that suit their skill and stay close to them when the task is new. I would check every isolation myself: their own locks and tags, and a dead test with a tester checked before and after. I would make sure they follow the fault-finding steps and do not change parts at random, and that they record each reading on the job sheet. I would check that spare parts match the original and that any part they are unsure about is shown to me first. I would inspect each repair before it is closed up and see that the dead tests after repair are done and recorded. Only the authorised person would energise for the function test. If a junior made a mistake, I would correct it straight away and explain why. At the end I would check the reports, clean-up and tool count, and report to the supervisor.
markingPoints: Briefs the team and matches tasks to skill
Checks each person's isolation and dead testing
Ensures logical fault-finding, correct parts and recorded readings
Inspects repairs and ensures post-repair tests and authorised energising
Corrects mistakes, checks reports and reports to the supervisor

essays.stem: A hotel asks you to set up a regular inspection and test programme for its portable electrical equipment. Explain what you would include and how Class I and Class II items are treated differently.
essays.modelAnswer: I would first make a register of every portable item, such as vacuum cleaners, floor polishers, irons, kettles, hair dryers, power tools and extension leads, each with an ID number. I would set how often each is checked, based on how hard it is used; items used in kitchens, laundries and outdoors need checks more often. Users would do a quick visual check before each use, looking for damaged cables, plugs and cases. A competent person would carry out formal inspections and tests. All items get a careful visual inspection. Class I items, which have an earthed metal case, also get an earth continuity test from the plug's earth pin to the case, and an insulation test. Class II items, which are double insulated and have no earth, get the visual inspection and an insulation test, but no earth continuity test. Each item that passes gets a dated label; failed items are tagged 'Do not use' and removed. Results go in the register, and faults found often show where training or better equipment is needed.
markingPoints: Register of items with ID numbers
Check intervals based on use and environment
User checks plus formal inspection and testing by a competent person
Class I: earth continuity and insulation tests; Class II: no earth test
Labels, removal of failed items and records

practical1.title: Diagnose and repair faults in portable power tools and extension leads (dead testing)
practical1.brief: The assessor gives your group a set of portable tools and leads with planted faults, for example an angle grinder with worn brushes, a drill with a broken conductor near the cable entry, a metal-cased tool with a loose earth, and an extension lead with a damaged plug or a wrong connection. Nothing is plugged in at any time. First, as a group, set up a repair bench: a 'quarantine' box for untested items, the test instruments, and a tool register. Each member takes at least one item and, with another member checking, carries out a visual inspection, then the dead tests: continuity of each conductor, earth continuity on Class I items, and an insulation resistance test at the voltage the instrument maker and tool maker say. Each member writes their readings on the test sheet, states the fault and its likely cause, repairs it with the correct parts (for example the maker's brushes, a new plug or a shortened cable), and repeats the tests to prove the repair. Items that cannot be repaired safely are tagged 'Do not use'. The instructor alone may carry out a short function run of repaired items. The group completes the register and a short repair report. Photograph each stage below.
materials: Portable tools and extension leads with planted faults (supplied by the assessor)
Insulation resistance tester and low-resistance ohmmeter or multimeter
Spare parts: correct carbon brushes, plugs, cable glands, flex of the right size
Screwdrivers, strippers, side cutters and a crimp tool
'Do not use' tags, pass labels, test sheets, register and repair report forms
photos: The repair bench set up, with the quarantine box and register
Each member's visual inspection, with the faults marked
A continuity or earth continuity test on a Class I item
An insulation resistance test, with the reading visible
The repair in progress, such as fitting new brushes or a plug
The completed test sheets, labels and repair report
checklist: Kept every item unplugged and under control throughout
Inspected the item fully before testing
Chose and connected the instrument correctly for each test
Recorded readings accurately and named the fault and cause
Repaired with the correct parts to a good standard
Retested after repair and labelled or tagged the item correctly
Completed their part of the register and report
safety: No item is plugged in; only the instructor may energise anything at the Centre
Discharge equipment after each insulation test before touching the terminals
Wear eye protection when cleaning commutators or working with springs
Keep sharp blades and discs off the tools during repair, and keep the bench tidy

practical2.title: Find and repair planted faults on a star-delta starter and control transformer training panel
practical2.brief: Your group works on the Centre's star-delta starter training panel, which includes a control transformer and is fed only through a training board that the group isolates. The assessor plants faults, for example a timer set wrongly or wired to the wrong contacts, an open-circuit delta contactor coil, a blown control transformer secondary fuse, a loose link on the motor terminal block or a faulty interlock contact. The assessor tells the group the symptom for each fault ('starts in star, then trips', 'no control supply', and so on). First the group applies a group lock-off with one padlock per member and proves the panel dead with a tester checked before and after. Then, with the schematic, the team leader shares out the faults. Each member plans their tests, carries out dead tests (continuity, coil resistance, fuse checks, winding resistance of the transformer, insulation to earth), finds the fault and repairs it, while another member checks and records. When all faults are cleared, the group completes a fault report and hands the panel to the instructor, who alone energises it for a function test while the group watches from behind the barrier. Photograph each stage below.
materials: Star-delta starter training panel with control transformer, timer and motor or motor simulator
Training board with lockable isolator, group lock hasp, padlocks and tags
Approved voltage tester and proving unit
Multimeter or low-resistance ohmmeter and insulation resistance tester
Schematic and wiring diagrams for the panel
Spare fuses, coil and links of the correct type; screwdrivers and ferrules
Fault-finding record sheet and fault report form
photos: The group lock-off, with every member's padlock and tag
The tester being proved before and after the dead test
Each member's test on the schematic, marked with readings
Each fault found and its repair
The completed fault-finding record and fault report
The instructor's function test, with the group behind the barrier
